fields.name: Machine Learning - II
fields.description:
BAI702 is the course code for Machine Learning-II, a 7th-semester core subject in the Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AIML / AI & ML)

Credits: 04
Total Marks: 100

� Module 1: Introduction to Well-Posed Learning Problems, Designing a Learning System, Concept Learning, Find-S, Version Spaces, and Candidate-Elimination Algorithm.
� Module 2: Learning Sets of Rules (Sequential Covering, FOIL Algorithm), Analytical Learning, and Explanation-Based Learning (EBL).
� Module 3: Ensemble Learning (AdaBoost, Random Forests) and Unsupervised Learning (K-Means Clustering).
� Module 4: Vector Quantisation, Self-Organizing Feature Maps (SOM), Box-Muller scheme, and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.
� Module 5: Bayesian Networks, Hidden Markov Models (HMM), and Probabilistic Inferences

fields.name: Data Security and Privacy
fields.description:
BAD703 is the course code for Data Security and Privacy, a 4-credit core theory subject typically offered in the 7th semester of B.E./B.Tech programs under Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) and affiliated engineering colleges (such as AI & DS / CSE).

� Module 1: Network security model, classical encryption techniques (Caesar, Monoalphabetic, Playfair, Hill, Polyalphabetic, One-time pad), steganography, and block ciphers like the Data Encryption Standard (DES).
� Modules 2�5: Advanced cryptographic algorithms (such as RSA and ECC), key management principles, web security, access control, and data privacy frameworks.

fields.name: Business Analytics
fields.description:
BAD714B is a 7th-semester undergraduate engineering course on Business Analytics offered under Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) for Artificial Intelligence and Data Science / related branches.

Credits: 3

� Module 1: Business Intelligence (BI), Analytics, Data Science, AI decision support frameworks, Conversational AI, and chatbots.
� Module 2: Descriptive Analytics I, data taxonomy, data preprocessing, Big Data, and statistical/regression modeling.
� Module 3: Descriptive Analytics II, Business Intelligence, Data Warehousing (architectures, administration, security), business reporting, data visualization, and dashboards.
� Module 4: Predictive Analytics I (data mining processes and algorithms) and Prescriptive Analytics (optimization, simulation, and spreadsheet decision modeling).
� Module 5: Predictive Analytics II, Text/Web/Social Media Analytics, Natural Language Processing (NLP), sentiment analysis, and web mining.

fields.name: Introduction to Non-Traditional Machining
fields.description:
BME755A is the course code for Non-Traditional Machining (NTM), a 7th-semester core subject in the Mechanical Engineering curriculum under the Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) scheme.

Credits: 03

Module 1: Introduction to Non-Traditional Machining� Need for NTM, comparison with traditional/conventional machining, and energy-based classifications (mechanical, electrochemical, chemical, thermal)

Module 2: Mechanical NTM Processes� USM (Ultrasonic Machining) and AJM (Abrasive Jet Machining) � working principles, setup, process parameters, and Material Removal Rate (MRR)

Module 3: Electrochemical & Chemical Processes� ECM (Electrochemical Machining), ECG, ECH, and CHM (Chemical Machining) including maskants and etchants

Module 4: Thermal & Electrical Discharge Processes� EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining), Wire EDM (WEDM), dielectric fluids, and PAM (Plasma Arc Machining).

Module 5: Beam Energy Processes� LBM (Laser Beam Machining) and EBM (Electron Beam Machining) � equipment setup, mechanisms, advantages, and limitations.

fields.title: Introduction to Machine Learning Approaches: Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning
fields.description: Core distinctions between supervised learning using labeled data, unsupervised learning objectives like clustering and density estimation, semi-supervised learning, and reinforcement learning applications.

fields.title: Shallow Learning vs. Deep Learning Architectures
fields.description: Comparison between shallow architectures and deep networks, focusing on automatic hierarchical feature extraction, multi-level abstraction, and eliminating the need for manual hand-designed feature extractors.

fields.title: Why Use Deep Learning and Real-World Applications
fields.description: Examination of why deep learning outperforms conventional machine learning algorithms in accuracy, generalization power, flexibility with nonlinear functions, and domain-oblivious deployment across various fields.

fields.title: How Deep Learning Works: Weights, Loss Functions, and Backpropagation
fields.description: The step-by-step mechanism of mapping inputs to targets via layered transformations, parameterizing layers with weights, measuring errors using objective/loss functions, and optimizing via backpropagation.

fields.title: Deep Learning Challenges and Neural Network Optimization
fields.description: Overview of intricate optimization hurdles in deep networks, including ill-conditioning, saddle points, vanishing and exploding gradients, empirical risk minimization, and minibatch stochastic gradient descent.

fields.title: Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
fields.description: Overview of supervised deep learning models, biological inspiration from the visual cortex, core concepts of local feature extraction, and performance on computer vision tasks.

fields.title: Evolution of Convolutional Neural Network Models
fields.description: Historical development of CNN architectures from LeNet to AlexNet, ZFNet, VGGNet, GoogLeNet, ResNet, Xception, SqueezeNet, and ShuffleNet, highlighting breakthroughs and architectural milestones

fields.title: Mathematical Foundation of Convolution Operation
fields.description: Mathematical formulations of 1D and 2D convolution operations, commutative properties, kernel flipping, and cross-correlation functions used in digital signal processing and deep learning libraries.

fields.title: Core Architecture of CNNs: Receptive Fields, Weight Sharing, and Pooling
fields.description: Key structural features of CNNs including local receptive fields, parameter reduction through weight sharing, and spatial size downsampling via max-pooling layers.

fields.title: Convolutional Layers, Hyperparameters, and Activation Functions
fields.description: Mechanics of convolutional layers, hyperparameters (filter size, number of filters, stride, zero padding), and non-linear activation functions including Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax, ReLU, and Swish.

fields.title: Fully Connected Layers and Dropout for Overfitting Control
fields.description: The transition from feature extraction to the classification stage using fully connected layers, softmax/SVM classifiers, and employing dropout layers to mitigate overfitting and improve model generalization.

fields.title: Training Convolutional Neural Networks and Forward/Backward Propagation Mathematics
fields.description: Formulating supervised deep learning training via loss minimization, detailed mathematical step-by-step framework for forward passes and backpropagation across convolutional layers (C1, C3, C5), max-pooling layers (P2, P4), fully connected layer (F6), and Softmax error derivation.

fields.title: Gradient Descent Optimization Variants: Batch, Stochastic, and Mini-batch
fields.description: Overview of gradient descent optimization techniques and their variants (Batch GD, Stochastic GD, and Mini-batch GD) highlighting trade-offs in memory usage, convergence stability, and learning rate dynamics.

fields.title: Advanced Adaptive Optimization Algorithms: AdaGrad, AdaDelta, RMSProp, and Adam
fields.description: Methods for faster convergence using adaptive learning rates, addressing decaying learning rates and gradient oscillations through AdaGrad, AdaDelta, RMSProp, and Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam).

fields.title: Challenges in Training Deep Networks: Vanishing Gradients, Data Size, and Overfitting
fields.description: Key obstacles encountered when training deep models, including the vanishing gradient problem in sigmoid/tanh networks, training dataset size and quality requirements, and managing overfitting versus underfitting via regularization and dropout

fields.title: Numerical Computation: Condition Numbers, Jacobians, and Hessians
fields.description: Fundamental mathematical concepts from numerical computation including ill-conditioning, Jacobians, Hessian matrices, second-order Taylor series approximations, eigenvalues, and second-order optimization methods like Newton's method.

fields.title: Introduction to Sequence Modeling and Unfolding Computational Graphs
fields.description: Fundamentals of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for processing sequential data via parameter sharing, unfolding recursive or recurrent computations into deep computational graphs, and representing dynamical systems.

fields.title: ecurrent Neural Network Architectures and Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)
fields.description: Forward propagation equations for standard RNNs, output design patterns, teacher forcing strategies, and computing gradients via Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT).

fields.title: RNNs as Directed Graphical Models and Context Conditioning
fields.description: Interpreting recurrent networks as directed graphical models for efficient sequence parametrization, modeling sequence length, and conditioning sequences on context (such as fixed-size vectors or input sequences).

fields.title: Bidirectional and Deep Recurrent Networks
fields.description: Capturing past and future context using bidirectional RNNs, extending models to multi-dimensional data, and introducing hierarchical depth and skip connections into recurrent architectures.

fields.title: Recursive Neural Networks
fields.description: Generalizing chain-like RNN structures to tree-structured computational graphs in recursive neural networks, reducing operation depth, and applications in natural language processing and parsing.

fields.title: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs)
fields.description: Overcoming vanishing/exploding gradients through gated RNNs, detailed mechanics of LSTM cells (input, forget, and output gates), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs).

fields.title: Introduction to Reinforcement Learning and Stateless Multi-Armed Bandits
fields.description: Overview of reward-driven trial-and-error learning inspired by biological intelligence and Herbert Simon's ant hypothesis, alongside stateless multi-armed bandit algorithms (na�ve, $\epsilon$-greedy, and upper bounding methods) addressing the exploration-exploitation trade-off.

fields.title: The Basic Framework of Reinforcement Learning: Markov Decision Processes
fields.description: Core components of reinforcement learning including agents, environments, actions, states, rewards, episodes, and Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), along with challenges like the credit-assignment problem.

fields.title: Value Discovery, Function Approximation, and Role of Deep Learning
fields.description: Transitioning from tabular methods and rote learning (such as simple tic-tac-toe state-action value tables) to deep neural networks as function approximators capable of generalizing experiences to vast, unseen state spaces like chess and Go.

fields.title: Case Studies in Deep Reinforcement Learning: AlphaGo, Alpha Zero, and Robotics
fields.description: Real-world applications of deep reinforcement learning showcasing championship-level gameplay in Go and chess via AlphaGo and Alpha Zero, self-learning robot locomotion (MuJoCo physics engine), and visuomotor skill acquisition.

fields.title: Conversational Systems, Self-Driving Cars, and Neural Architecture Search
fields.description: Advanced reinforcement learning and imitation learning applications including end-to-end negotiation chatbots, autonomous self-driving car control systems (NVIDIA architecture), and inferring neural network architectures using recurrent controller networks.

fields.title: Introduction to Machine Learning and Well-Posed Learning Problems
fields.description: Definition of machine learning as improving performance through experience, real-world applications including speech recognition and autonomous vehicles, and formulating well-posed learning problems by identifying tasks ($T$), performance measures ($P$), and training experience ($E$).

fields.title: Designing a Learning System: Training Experience and Target Functions
fields.description: Design choices involving training experience types (direct vs. indirect feedback and the credit assignment problem), controlling training sequences, and selecting operational target functions over nonoperational recursive definitions.

fields.title: Target Function Representation, Training Estimation, and LMS Weight Update Rule
fields.description: Representing target functions as linear combinations of board features, estimating training values from successor states, and minimizing squared error using the Least Mean Squares (LMS) gradient descent training rule.

fields.title: Architecture of Learning Systems: Performance System, Critic, Generalizer, and Experiment Generator
fields.description: The four generic modules of learning systems comprising the Performance System, Critic, Generalizer, and Experiment Generator, along with viewing machine learning as searching a vast hypothesis space.

fields.title: Concept Learning, Hypothesis Spaces, and General-to-Specific Ordering
fields.description: Formulating concept learning as inferring boolean-valued functions from examples, the inductive learning hypothesis, and organizing hypothesis space search using the general-to-specific partial ordering ($\ge_g$).

fields.title: FIND-S Algorithm and Version Spaces with CANDIDATE-ELIMINATION
fields.description: The FIND-S algorithm for finding maximally specific consistent hypotheses, defining version spaces and the List-Then-Eliminate algorithm, general ($G$) and specific ($S$) boundary sets, and the CANDIDATE-ELIMINATION algorithm.

fields.title: Inductive Bias in Machine Learning
fields.description: The fundamental need for inductive bias in generalizing beyond training data, analyzing biased versus unbiased (power set) hypothesis spaces, the futility of bias-free learning, and modeling inductive learning systems using equivalent deductive systems.

fields.title: Introduction to Learning Sets of Rules and First-Order Horn Clauses
fields.description: Overview of learning sets of if-then rules, expressive first-order Horn clauses containing variables, Inductive Logic Programming (ILP), and Prolog-like logic programming representations.

fields.title: Sequential Covering Algorithms and LEARN-ONE-RULE
fields.description: Sequential covering algorithms that iteratively learn one rule at a time, remove covered positive examples, and learn disjunctive sets of rules using a LEARN-ONE-RULE subroutine.

fields.title: General-to-Specific Beam Search and the CN2 Algorithm
fields.description: Implementing LEARN-ONE-RULE via general-to-specific beam search (as used in CN2), greedily adding attribute tests, and evaluating candidates using entropy or PERFORMANCE measures.

fields.title: Rule Learning Summary: Design Dimensions and Performance Measures
fields.description: Key dimensions of rule learning algorithms including sequential vs. simultaneous covering, search direction, generate-and-test vs. example-driven search, rule post-pruning, and performance metrics (relative frequency, m-estimate, entropy).

fields.title: Learning First-Order Rules with FOIL (First-Order Inductive Learner)
fields.description: Extending rule learning to first-order Horn clauses using FOIL, generating candidate specializations with variables, guiding search with Foil Gain, and learning recursive rule sets.

fields.title: Induction as Inverted Deduction and Inverting Resolution
fields.description: Formulating machine learning as inverse entailment ($B \wedge h \wedge x_i \vdash f(x_i)$), inverting the resolution rule (CIGOL program), and managing first-order resolution with unifying substitutions.

fields.title: Generalization, theta-Subsumption, Entailment, and PROGOL
fields.description: Comparing more-general-than , \theta-subsumption, and logical entailment, along with the PROGOL system combining inverse entailment with a bounded general-to-specific search.

fields.title: Introduction to Ensemble Learning and Majority Voting
fields.description: Overview of ensemble methods combining multiple classifiers to improve generalization performance, medical diagnosis analogy, and binary classification properties using majority voting.
